title: Azure Storage redundancy: LRS, ZRS, GRS, RA-GRS, GZRS, RA-GZRS
learningObjective: Choose and change a storage account's redundancy, based on what failure you must survive, whether you need to read during an outage, how much data you can lose, and feature limits. Know what happens in each failure.

prerequisites.text: Regions, region pairs and availability zones (AZ-900)

foundation: Azure always keeps at least three copies of your data. Redundancy settings decide where those copies live.

LRS keeps three copies in one datacenter. ZRS spreads three copies across three availability zones in one region. GRS and GZRS do the same in the primary region and also send a copy to a second region hundreds of kilometres away.
The 'RA-' versions (RA-GRS, RA-GZRS) also let you read from the second region at any time. Without RA-, the secondary copy is there for disaster recovery but you cannot read it until a failover.

Copies inside one region are written at the same time (synchronously). The copy to the second region is sent a little later (asynchronously), so the very latest writes can be lost if the primary region is destroyed.
engineer: Writes in the main region: a write only counts as done when all three copies are saved at the same time. LRS keeps the three copies in one datacenter. ZRS spreads them across three zones.
How durable each option is (per year): LRS at least 11 nines; ZRS at least 12 nines; GRS, RA-GRS, GZRS and RA-GZRS at least 16 nines.

Copying to the second region: this happens in the background (asynchronously) to the paired region. It's usually less than 15 minutes behind, but there's no guarantee (no SLA). That gap is your RPO: the data you could lose.
Last Sync Time: the property geoReplicationStats.lastSyncTime tells you up to when the second region is complete. Anything written after it could be lost in a disaster.

The second region is always LRS: after an unplanned failover that you start, the account is LRS in the new main region. You must turn geo-redundancy on again, which copies everything again and costs data transfer.
RA- means you can read the second copy: RA-GRS and RA-GZRS give a read-only address, <account>-secondary.blob.core.windows.net. Your app must be built to use it, for example by retrying reads there.
Feature limits: premium block blob and premium file share accounts only support LRS and ZRS (no second region); the archive tier only works on LRS, GRS and RA-GRS, not on ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS.

Changing redundancy: switching between LRS, GRS and RA-GRS, or between ZRS, GZRS and RA-GZRS, is a simple setting change. Adding or removing zones (for example LRS to ZRS) needs a conversion, requested on the Redundancy page, or a manual move. Zone options only exist in regions that have availability zones.

example.title: Choosing redundancy for three kinds of data
body: Build files you can make again: LRS. It's the cheapest, and losing them is annoying, not a disaster.
Order documents for an app running across zones in West Europe: ZRS. If one zone fails, the data can still be read and written, just like the app keeps running.

A legal archive that must survive a whole region going down, and be readable during it: RA-GZRS if you don't need the archive tier. If you need the archive tier, RA-GRS, because archive doesn't work on zone-redundant accounts.

prerequisites: A region with availability zones, for ZRS, GZRS and RA-GZRS
A general-purpose v2 account, for the geo-zone options
permissions: Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/write (Storage Account Contributor or Contributor) to change redundancy (the account SKU)
limits: Premium block blob and file share accounts: LRS or ZRS only
Archive tier: LRS, GRS and RA-GRS only
No guarantee on geo-copy delay; usually under 15 minutes
portal: Storage accounts > Create > Basics > Redundancy: choose LRS, ZRS, GRS or GZRS; tick 'Make read access to data available in the event of regional unavailability' for RA-.
Existing account > Data management > Redundancy: change the option, view Last Sync Time and the secondary endpoints.
configuration.cli:
az storage account create -g rg-data -n stcvadocs01 -l westeurope --kind StorageV2 --sku Standard_GZRS
az storage account update -g rg-data -n stcvadocs01 --sku Standard_RAGZRS
az storage account show -g rg-data -n stcvadocs01 --expand geoReplicationStats \
  --query "{sku:sku.name, lastSync:geoReplicationStats.lastSyncTime, secondary:secondaryEndpoints.blob}"
az storage account failover -g rg-data -n stcvadocs01
configuration.powershell:
New-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcvadocs01 -Location westeurope -Kind StorageV2 -SkuName Standard_GZRS
Set-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcvadocs01 -SkuName Standard_RAGZRS
(Get-AzStorageAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcvadocs01 -IncludeGeoReplicationStats).GeoReplicationStats.LastSyncTime
Invoke-AzStorageAccountFailover -ResourceGroupName rg-data -Name stcvadocs01

lab.objective: Prove which redundancy options survive each failure domain, and where data loss is still possible.
steps: Select LRS, write data, then fail the datacenter/zone. Note availability and loss risk.
Select ZRS and fail a zone, then fail the region.
Select GRS and fail the region. Note that reads stop until failover and recent writes can be lost.
Select RA-GZRS and fail the region. Reads continue from the secondary endpoint.
expected: ZRS: survives a zone, not a region.
Geo options: data-loss risk is 'recent writes', never zero.

validation.text: Read from the secondary under an RA- option during a region outage

failureScenarios: Assuming GRS reads continue during an outage without RA-
lab.cost: None. Runs entirely in the browser. Real geo-redundant accounts cost more per GB and incur replication bandwidth charges.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't pick ZRS or GZRS when creating an account.
troubleshooting.cause: The region has no availability zones, or the account type doesn't support zones.
troubleshooting.fix: Pick a region with zones, or an account type that supports ZRS.

troubleshooting.symptom: Setting a blob to Archive fails on a GZRS account.
troubleshooting.cause: Archive doesn't work with ZRS, GZRS or RA-GZRS.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Cool or Cold, or keep archive data in an LRS, GRS or RA-GRS account.

troubleshooting.cause: The account is GRS or GZRS without RA-, or the blob hasn't been copied yet (written after Last Sync Time).
troubleshooting.fix: Switch to RA-, and check Last Sync Time.

troubleshooting.symptom: After a failover, the account shows LRS.
troubleshooting.cause: This is normal: after an unplanned failover the new main region is LRS.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn GRS or GZRS back on after the incident. Plan for the time and cost of copying everything again.

comparisons.service: Azure Backup / blob soft delete / versioning
comparisons.difference: Redundancy protects against broken hardware or a lost site. It doesn't protect against deletes or corruption, because those are copied everywhere. Soft delete, versioning and backups do.
Copies block blobs between containers in accounts you choose, in any region. Geo-redundancy copies the whole account to its fixed paired region.
S3 Standard keeps data in at least three zones by default. Copying to another region needs S3 Replication rules, not an account setting.

misconceptions.myth: With GRS, no data is lost if the region fails.
misconceptions.reality: No. Copying is in the background, so writes after the Last Sync Time can be lost.

misconceptions.myth: With GRS you can read the second copy any time.
misconceptions.reality: No. Only RA-GRS and RA-GZRS let you read it without a failover.

misconceptions.myth: ZRS protects you if a whole region goes down.
misconceptions.reality: No. All ZRS copies are in one region.
No. Deletes are copied too. Use soft delete, versioning, point-in-time restore or backups.

architectureDecisions: Match storage to compute: if your app runs across zones, use ZRS or GZRS. Otherwise a zone failure takes out your storage even though the app survives.
Watch Last Sync Time: if data loss matters, it shows your real risk, not the usual 15 minutes.
Only pay for RA- if your app reads the second copy: otherwise you pay for something you never use.

walkthrough.subtitle: Choose how many copies of your data Azure keeps, and how far apart.
learn: LRS: three copies in one datacenter
GRS and GZRS: a copy in another region

steps.label: Disasters
steps.title: Disks fail, buildings flood, regions go down
body: How much loss can your data survive? The answer decides your redundancy option and its price.

steps.label: LRS
steps.title: LRS: cheapest, one building
body: Locally redundant storage keeps three copies in one datacenter. It survives a disk or server failure, but not a fire or flood in that building.

steps.label: ZRS
steps.title: ZRS: three zones in one region
body: Zone-redundant storage spreads three copies across three availability zones (separate buildings with their own power). It survives a whole datacenter going down.

steps.label: GRS
steps.title: GRS and GZRS: another region too
body: Geo-redundant storage (GRS) = LRS in the primary region plus an asynchronous copy to the paired region. GZRS = ZRS in the primary plus the copy in the secondary region.
The secondary copy is not readable until you fail over, unless you choose the RA- version.

steps.label: RA-
steps.title: RA-GRS and RA-GZRS: read the copy any time
body: Read-access versions give you a second endpoint (accountname-secondary) to read data from the secondary region at any time, even when the primary is healthy.

steps.label: Change
steps.title: Changing redundancy later
body: Switching between LRS, GRS and RA-GRS is a simple setting change. Moving to or from zone redundancy (ZRS, GZRS) is a conversion that Azure performs in the background, or a data copy for some cases.

callout.text: Premium accounts and some features (for example Premium file shares) do not support geo-redundancy.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Redundancy
body: More distance, more safety, more cost.
recap: GRS / GZRS: plus an async copy in the paired region
LRS↔GRS is a setting; zone changes are conversions

handsOn.title: Change a storage account from LRS to RA-GRS
handsOn.cost: Cents. Geo-redundancy costs a little more per GB; with no data it is close to zero.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.
A storage account in rg-az104-lab: Standard performance, LRS redundancy, default settings. Name it st<yourinitials><number> (lowercase letters and numbers only, globally unique).

steps.do: Open the storage account > Data management > Redundancy.
steps.see: Current redundancy LRS and a map with one location.

steps.do: Change the redundancy setting to Read-access geo-redundant storage (RA-GRS). Save.
steps.see: The map now shows a primary and a secondary region, with status Available for both after a short while.
Secondary endpoints such as https://<name>-secondary.blob.core.windows.net, because it is RA-GRS.

steps.do: Back on Redundancy, open the redundancy list again.
steps.see: Zone-redundant options may require a conversion. Read the message, but do not convert.

steps.do: Change back to LRS and Save.
steps.see: A single location on the map again.

check: You saw the secondary region and the -secondary endpoint.
cleanup: When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
